sanskrit: avināśo 'sya sattvasya niyato yadi bhārata bhittvā śarīraṃ bhūtānām ahiṃsāṃ pratipadyate
english: If, O Bhārata, the imperishability of this living essence is settled and certain, then in cleaving the body of creatures one in truth attains to non-injury.

sanskrit: labdhvāpi pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ sahasthāvarajaṅgamām mamatvaṃ yasya naiva syāt kiṃ tayā sa kariṣyati
english: Even having gained the whole earth, with all that is unmoving and moving upon it, what will he do with it, in whom there is no sense of "mine"?

sanskrit: atha vā vasataḥ pārtha vane vanyena jīvataḥ mamatā yasya dravyeṣu mṛtyor āsye sa vartate
english: Or again, O Pārtha, though a man dwell in the forest and live on its wild produce, if the sense of "mine" toward possessions remains in him, he abides within the very jaws of death.

sanskrit: bāhyāntarāṇāṃ śatrūṇāṃ svabhāvaṃ paśya bhārata yan na paśyati tad bhūtaṃ mucyate sa mahābhayāt
english: Look, O Bhārata, upon the nature of one's enemies, outer and inner alike; the being who does not perceive that nature is freed from the great fear.

sanskrit: kāmātmānaṃ na praśaṃsanti loke; na cākāmāt kā cid asti pravṛttiḥ dānaṃ hi vedādhyayanaṃ tapaś ca; kāmena karmāṇi ca vaidikāni
english: In the world men do not praise the one who is wholly given over to desire; yet without desire there is no undertaking at all. For giving, the study of the Veda, austerity, and the rites prescribed in the Veda — these are all set in motion by desire.

sanskrit: vrataṃ yajñān niyamān dhyānayogān; kāmena yo nārabhate viditvā yad yad dhy ayaṃ kāmayate sa dharmo; na yo dharmo niyamas tasya mūlam
english: There is no man who, having understood, undertakes vows, sacrifices, observances, and the practice of meditation otherwise than through desire. Whatever this desire seeks, that becomes the duty pursued; for it is not duty, but restraint of desire, that is the root of such striving.

sanskrit: atra gāthāḥ kāmagītāḥ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ śṛṇu saṃkīrtyamānās tā nikhilena yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this theme the knowers of old recite verses sung by Desire itself; hear them, O Yudhiṣṭhira, recited now in their entirety.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ śakyo 'nupāyena hantuṃ bhūtena kena cit yo māṃ prayatate hantuṃ jñātvā praharaṇe balam tasya tasmin praharaṇe punaḥ prādurbhavāmy aham
english: "I cannot be slain by any creature through means unfit for the task. Whoever, knowing where strength lies, strives to slay me by striking — in that very striking I, Desire, arise again within him."

sanskrit: yo māṃ prayatate hantuṃ yajñair vividhadakṣiṇaiḥ jaṅgameṣv iva karmātmā punaḥ prādurbhavāmy aham
english: "Whoever strives to slay me by sacrifices with their manifold fees, in him, as one whose self is bent on action, I arise again, as it were among moving things."

sanskrit: yo māṃ prayatate hantuṃ vedair vedāntasādhanaiḥ sthāvareṣv iva śāntātmā tasya prādurbhavāmy aham
english: "Whoever strives to slay me by the Vedas and the disciplines of the Vedānta, in him, his self grown calm, I arise again, as it were among unmoving things."

sanskrit: yo māṃ prayatate hantuṃ dhṛtyā satyaparākramaḥ bhāvo bhavāmi tasyāhaṃ sa ca māṃ nāvabudhyate
english: "Whoever, with truth for his valor, strives to slay me by steadfast resolve — of him I become the very inclination of his heart, and he does not perceive me."

sanskrit: yo māṃ prayatate hantuṃ tapasā saṃśitavrataḥ tatas tapasi tasyātha punaḥ prādurbhavāmy aham
english: "Whoever, his vows made keen, strives to slay me by austerity, then in that very austerity of his I arise again."

sanskrit: yo māṃ prayatate hantuṃ mokṣam āsthāya paṇḍitaḥ tasya mokṣaratisthasya nṛtyāmi ca hasāmi ca avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānām aham ekaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: "Whoever, a learned man, strives to slay me by taking his stand upon liberation — at him, fixed in the joy of release, I dance and I laugh; for I alone am eternal, not to be slain by any being."

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam api taṃ kāmaṃ yajñair vividhadakṣiṇaiḥ dharmaṃ kuru mahārāja tatra te sa bhaviṣyati
english: Therefore do you too, O great king, by sacrifices with their manifold fees, turn that very desire into duty; there it shall serve your purpose.

sanskrit: yajasva vājimedhena vidhivad dakṣiṇāvatā anyaiś ca vividhair yajñaiḥ samṛddhair āptadakṣiṇaiḥ
english: Offer the Horse Sacrifice according to the rule, with its due fees, and other manifold sacrifices besides, abundant and complete in their gifts.

sanskrit: mā te vyathāstu nihatān bandhūn vīkṣya punaḥ punaḥ na śakyās te punar draṣṭuṃ ye hatāsmin raṇājire
english: Let there be no anguish in you as you gaze again and again upon your slain kinsmen; those who fell on this field of battle can never be seen again.

sanskrit: sa tvam iṣṭvā mahāyajñaiḥ samṛddhair āptadakṣiṇaiḥ loke kīrtiṃ parāṃ prāpya gatim agryāṃ gamiṣyasi
english: You, then, having worshipped with great sacrifices, abundant and complete in their gifts, will win the highest renown in the world and attain the supreme goal.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ bahuvidhair vākyair munibhis tais tapodhanaiḥ samāśvasyata rājarṣir hatabandhur yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus, by manifold sayings of those sages rich in austerity, was the royal sage Yudhiṣṭhira, his kinsmen slain, comforted and consoled.

sanskrit: so 'nunīto bhagavatā viṣṭaraśravasā svayam dvaipāyanena kṛṣṇena devasthānena cābhibhūḥ
english: That sovereign was won over by the blessed Viṣṭaraśravas himself, by Dvaipāyana, by Kṛṣṇa, and by Devasthāna.

sanskrit: nāradenātha bhīmena nakulena ca pārthivaḥ kṛṣṇayā sahadevena vijayena ca dhīmatā
english: The king was consoled too by Nārada, by Bhīma, by Nakula, by Kṛṣṇā, by Sahadeva, and by the wise Vijaya.

sanskrit: anyaiś ca puruṣavyāghrair brāhmaṇaiḥ śāstradṛṣṭibhiḥ vyajahāc chokajaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃtāpaṃ caiva mānasam
english: And by other tigers among men, by brāhmaṇas whose insight rested on the scriptures, he cast off the grief born of sorrow and the burning anguish of his mind.

sanskrit: arcayām āsa devāṃś ca brāhmaṇāṃś ca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kṛtvātha pretakāryāṇi bandhūnāṃ sa punar nṛpaḥ anvaśāsata dharmātmā pṛthivīṃ sāgarāmbarām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira honored the gods and the brāhmaṇas, and having performed the funeral rites for his kinsmen, that king, righteous of soul, once more ruled the earth girdled by the sea.

sanskrit: praśāntacetāḥ kauravyaḥ svarājyaṃ prāpya kevalam vyāsaṃ ca nāradaṃ caiva tāṃś cānyān abravīn nṛpaḥ
english: His mind grown calm, the Kaurava king, having gained his undivided kingdom, spoke to Vyāsa and Nārada and those others.

sanskrit: āśvāsito 'haṃ prāg vṛddhair bhavadbhir munipuṃgavaiḥ na sūkṣmam api me kiṃ cid vyalīkam iha vidyate
english: "I have been consoled by you, elders and bulls among sages; not even the slightest trace of false grief remains in me now."

sanskrit: arthaś ca sumahān prāpto yena yakṣyāmi devatāḥ puraskṛtyeha bhavataḥ samāneṣyāmahe makham
english: "Great wealth has been won, by which I shall worship the gods; placing you here at the head, we shall bring the sacrifice to completion."

sanskrit: himavantaṃ tvayā guptā gamiṣyāmaḥ pitāmaha bahvāścaryo hi deśaḥ sa śrūyate dvijasattama
english: "Guarded by you, grandsire, we shall journey to the Himavat; for that land, O best of the twice-born, is said to be full of wonders."

sanskrit: tathā bhagavatā citraṃ kalyāṇaṃ bahu bhāṣitam devarṣiṇā nāradena devasthānena caiva ha
english: Likewise much that was wondrous and salutary was spoken by the blessed one, by the divine sage Nārada, and by Devasthāna.

sanskrit: nābhāgadheyaḥ puruṣaḥ kaś cid evaṃvidhān gurūn labhate vyasanaṃ prāpya suhṛdaḥ sādhusaṃmatān
english: No man devoid of good fortune ever obtains, when calamity befalls him, such teachers as these — friends esteemed by the good.

sanskrit: evam uktās tu te rājñā sarva eva maharṣayaḥ abhyanujñāpya rājānaṃ tathobhau kṛṣṇaphalgunau paśyatām eva sarveṣāṃ tatraivādarśanaṃ yayuḥ
english: Thus addressed by the king, all those great sages, having taken their leave of him and of both Kṛṣṇa and Phalguna, vanished from sight then and there, before the eyes of all.

sanskrit: tato dharmasuto rājā tatraivopāviśat prabhuḥ evaṃ nātimahān kālaḥ sa teṣām abhyavartata
english: Then the king, the son of Dharma, the lord, sat down there; and thus no very long time passed for them.

sanskrit: kurvatāṃ śaucakarmāṇi bhīṣmasya nidhane tadā mahādānāni viprebhyo dadatām aurdhvadaihikam
english: As they performed the rites of purification at the death of Bhīṣma, bestowing great gifts upon the brāhmaṇas as offerings for the departed,

sanskrit: bhīṣmakarṇapurogāṇāṃ kurūṇāṃ kurunandana sahito dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa pradadāv aurdhvadaihikam
english: for the Kurus led by Bhīṣma and Karṇa, O delight of the Kurus, the king, together with Dhṛtarāṣṭra, bestowed the offerings for the departed.

sanskrit: tato dattvā bahu dhanaṃ viprebhyaḥ pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ puraskṛtya viveśa gajasāhvayam
english: Then, having given much wealth to the brāhmaṇas, the bull of the Pāṇḍavas, placing Dhṛtarāṣṭra at the head, entered the city named for the elephant.

sanskrit: sa samāśvāsya pitaraṃ prajñācakṣuṣam īśvaram anvaśād vai sa dharmātmā pṛthivīṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: Having consoled his father, the lord whose sight was wisdom, that righteous-souled one ruled the earth together with his brothers.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca vijite pāṇḍaveyais tu praśānte ca dvijottama rāṣṭre kiṃ cakratur vīrau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: Janamejaya said: When the realm had been won by the Pāṇḍavas and brought to peace, O best of the twice-born, what did the two heroes Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya then do?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vijite pāṇḍaveyais tu praśānte ca viśāṃ pate rāṣṭre babhūvatur hṛṣṭau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the realm had been won by the Pāṇḍavas and brought to peace, O lord of peoples, Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya grew glad of heart.

sanskrit: vijahrāte mudā yuktau divi deveśvarāv iva tau vaneṣu vicitreṣu parvatānāṃ ca sānuṣu
english: Joined in joy, those two disported themselves like the two lords of the gods in heaven, in lovely forests and upon the slopes of mountains,

sanskrit: śaileṣu ramaṇīyeṣu palvaleṣu nadīṣu ca caṅkramyamāṇau saṃhṛṣṭāv aśvināv iva nandane
english: upon delightful crags, by pools and by rivers, wandering full of delight, like the two Aśvins in the Nandana grove.

sanskrit: indraprasthe mahātmānau remāte kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau praviśya tāṃ sabhāṃ ramyāṃ vijahrāte ca bhārata
english: In Indraprastha the two great souls, Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava, took their pleasure, and entering that lovely assembly hall they disported themselves, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatra yuddhakathāś citrāḥ parikleśāṃś ca pārthiva kathāyoge kathāyoge kathayām āsatus tadā
english: There, O king, in the course of one tale and another, they recounted at that time the wondrous stories of the war and the hardships they had borne.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca vaṃśāṃs tāv āhatus tadā prīyamāṇau mahātmānau purāṇāv ṛṣisattamau
english: The two great souls, ancient and best of sages, taking delight in one another, then rehearsed the lineages of the seers and of the gods.

sanskrit: madhurās tu kathāś citrāś citrārthapadaniścayāḥ niścayajñaḥ sa pārthāya kathayām āsa keśavaḥ
english: And Keśava, knower of all certainties, recounted to Pārtha tales sweet and wondrous, settled in subtle meaning and well-chosen word.

sanskrit: putraśokābhisaṃtaptaṃ jñātīnāṃ ca sahasraśaḥ kathābhiḥ śamayām āsa pārthaṃ śaurir janārdanaḥ
english: With his tales, the descendant of Śūra, Janārdana, soothed Pārtha, who was scorched by grief for his son and for kinsmen by the thousand.

sanskrit: sa tam āśvāsya vidhivad vidhānajño mahātapāḥ apahṛtyātmano bhāraṃ viśaśrāmeva sātvataḥ
english: Having duly consoled him, the Sātvata, knower of the right ordering and great in austere power, lifted as it were the burden from his own heart and took his rest.

sanskrit: tataḥ kathānte govindo guḍākeśam uvāca ha sāntvayañ ślakṣṇayā vācā hetuyuktam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then at the close of their talk Govinda spoke to Guḍākeśa, soothing him with gentle speech, these words full of sound reason.

sanskrit: vijiteyaṃ dharā kṛtsnā savyasācin paraṃtapa tvadbāhubalam āśritya rājñā dharmasutena ha
english: "This whole earth has been conquered, O Savyasācin, scorcher of foes, by the king, the son of Dharma, leaning upon the strength of your arms."

sanskrit: asapatnāṃ mahīṃ bhuṅkte dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmasenaprabhāvena yamayoś ca narottama
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira, the king of righteousness, enjoys the earth free of all rivals, O best of men, by the might of Bhīmasena and of the twins."

sanskrit: dharmeṇa rājñā dharmajña prāptaṃ rājyam akaṇṭakam dharmeṇa nihataḥ saṃkhye sa ca rājā suyodhanaḥ
english: "By righteousness, O knower of righteousness, the king has gained a kingdom without a thorn; by righteousness too was King Suyodhana slain in battle."

sanskrit: adharmarucayo lubdhāḥ sadā cāpriyavādinaḥ dhārtarāṣṭrā durātmānaḥ sānubandhā nipātitāḥ
english: "The sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — delighting in unrighteousness, greedy, ever speaking hateful words, evil of soul — have been laid low together with all their followers."

sanskrit: praśāntām akhilāṃ pārtha pṛthivīṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ bhuṅkte dharmasuto rājā tvayā guptaḥ kurūdvaha
english: "The whole earth brought to peace, O Pārtha, the lord of the earth, King Dharma's son, enjoys, guarded by you, O foremost of the Kurus."

sanskrit: rame cāhaṃ tvayā sārdham araṇyeṣv api pāṇḍava kim u yatra jano 'yaṃ vai pṛthā cāmitrakarśana
english: "I take delight in your company even in the wild forests, O Pāṇḍava — how much more here, where these our people are, and Pṛthā too, O wearer-down of foes."

sanskrit: yatra dharmasuto rājā yatra bhīmo mahābalaḥ yatra mādravatīputrau ratis tatra parā mama
english: "Where King Dharma's son is, where Bhīma of mighty strength is, where the two sons of Mādravatī are — there is my highest delight."

sanskrit: tathaiva svargakalpeṣu sabhoddeśeṣu bhārata ramaṇīyeṣu puṇyeṣu sahitasya tvayānagha
english: "And so it is in these assembly halls like very heaven, O Bhārata, delightful and holy, when I am here together with you, O sinless one."

sanskrit: kālo mahāṃs tv atīto me śūraputram apaśyataḥ baladevaṃ ca kauravya tathānyān vṛṣṇipuṃgavān
english: "But a long time has now passed for me without sight of the son of Śūra, and of Baladeva, O Kaurava, and of the other bulls among the Vṛṣṇis."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ gantum abhīpsāmi purīṃ dvāravatīṃ prati rocatāṃ gamanaṃ mahyaṃ tavāpi puruṣarṣabha
english: "I therefore wish to journey toward the city of Dvāravatī; let my going be approved by you also, O bull among men."

sanskrit: ukto bahuvidhaṃ rājā tatra tatra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sa ha bhīṣmeṇa yady uktam asmābhiḥ śokakārite
english: "King Yudhiṣṭhira has been counseled in many ways, time and again, by Bhīṣma — and by us too, when he was overcome by grief."

sanskrit: śiṣṭo yudhiṣṭhiro 'smābhiḥ śāstā sann api pāṇḍavaḥ tena tac ca vacaḥ samyag gṛhītaṃ sumahātmanā
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira the Pāṇḍava, though himself a teacher, was instructed by us, and that counsel was rightly received by that great soul."

sanskrit: dharmaputre hi dharmajñe kṛtajñe satyavādini satyaṃ dharmo matiś cāgryā sthitiś ca satataṃ sthirā
english: "For in Dharma's son — knower of righteousness, grateful, speaker of truth — there is truth, there is righteousness, there is supreme understanding, and a steadfastness forever firm."

sanskrit: tad gatvā taṃ mahātmānaṃ yadi te rocate 'rjuna asmadgamanasaṃyuktaṃ vaco brūhi janādhipam
english: "Therefore, Arjuna, if it please you, go to that great soul, the lord of men, and speak to him the word concerning our departure."

sanskrit: na hi tasyāpriyaṃ kuryāṃ prāṇatyāge 'py upasthite kuto gantuṃ mahābāho purīṃ dvāravatīṃ prati
english: "For I would do nothing displeasing to him, even were the loss of life at hand — how much less would I go toward the city of Dvāravatī against his wish, O mighty-armed one."

sanskrit: sarvaṃ tv idam ahaṃ pārtha tvatprītihitakāmyayā bravīmi satyaṃ kauravya na mithyaitat kathaṃ cana
english: "All this, O Pārtha, I speak out of desire for your joy and your good; it is the truth, O Kaurava, and in no way is it false."

sanskrit: prayojanaṃ ca nirvṛttam iha vāse mamārjuna dhārtarāṣṭro hato rājā sabalaḥ sapadānugaḥ
english: "And the purpose of my dwelling here is accomplished, Arjuna: the king, son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, has been slain, together with his army and his followers."

sanskrit: pṛthivī ca vaśe tāta dharmaputrasya dhīmataḥ sthitā samudravasanā saśailavanakānanā citā ratnair bahuvidhaiḥ kururājasya pāṇḍava
english: "And the earth, my friend, sea-girt, with its mountains, woods, and forests, is set beneath the sway of the wise son of Dharma, heaped with jewels of many kinds — the earth of the Kuru king, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: dharmeṇa rājā dharmajñaḥ pātu sarvāṃ vasuṃdharām upāsyamāno bahubhiḥ siddhaiś cāpi mahātmabhiḥ stūyamānaś ca satataṃ bandibhir bharatarṣabha
english: "By righteousness let the king, the knower of righteousness, protect all the bounteous earth — attended by many perfected great souls and ever praised by the bards, O bull of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: tan mayā saha gatvādya rājānaṃ kuruvardhanam āpṛccha kuruśārdūla gamanaṃ dvārakāṃ prati
english: "So come with me now and ask leave of the king, the increaser of the Kurus, O tiger of the Kurus, for the journey toward Dvārakā."

sanskrit: idaṃ śarīraṃ vasu yac ca me gṛhe; niveditaṃ pārtha sadā yudhiṣṭhire priyaś ca mānyaś ca hi me yudhiṣṭhiraḥ; sadā kurūṇām adhipo mahāmatiḥ
english: "This body, and whatever wealth is in my house, has always, O Pārtha, been dedicated to Yudhiṣṭhira; for Yudhiṣṭhira, the high-minded lord of the Kurus, is ever dear to me and honored by me."

sanskrit: prayojanaṃ cāpi nivāsakāraṇe; na vidyate me tvad ṛte mahābhuja sthitā hi pṛthvī tava pārtha śāsane; guroḥ suvṛttasya yudhiṣṭhirasya ha
english: "And for dwelling here I have no purpose left, O mighty-armed, save you alone; for the earth, O Pārtha, abides under the rule of your venerable, well-conducted elder, Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: itīdam uktaṃ sa tadā mahātmanā; janārdanenāmitavikramo 'rjunaḥ tatheti kṛcchrād iva vācam īrayaj; janārdanaṃ saṃpratipūjya pārthiva
english: Thus addressed by the great soul Janārdana, Arjuna of measureless valor, O king, uttered with difficulty, as it were, the word "So be it," and paid full honor to Janārdana.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca sabhāyāṃ vasatos tasyāṃ nihatyārīn mahātmanoḥ keśavārjunayoḥ kā nu kathā samabhavad dvija
english: Janamejaya said: As the two great souls, Keśava and Arjuna, dwelt in that hall, their foes slain, what discourse, O brāhmaṇa, then arose between them?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kṛṣṇena sahitaḥ pārthaḥ svarājyaṃ prāpya kevalam tasyāṃ sabhāyāṃ ramyāyāṃ vijahāra mudā yutaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Together with Kṛṣṇa, Pārtha, having gained his undivided kingdom, disported himself with joy in that lovely hall.

sanskrit: tataḥ kaṃ cit sabhoddeśaṃ svargoddeśasamaṃ nṛpa yadṛcchayā tau muditau jagmatuḥ svajanāvṛtau
english: Then, O king, those two, glad of heart and surrounded by their own people, came by chance to a certain quarter of the hall, like some quarter of heaven.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratītaḥ kṛṣṇena sahitaḥ pāṇḍavo 'rjunaḥ nirīkṣya tāṃ sabhāṃ ramyām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then the Pāṇḍava Arjuna, content, together with Kṛṣṇa, gazing upon that lovely hall, spoke these words.

sanskrit: viditaṃ te mahābāho saṃgrāme samupasthite māhātmyaṃ devakīmātas tac ca te rūpam aiśvaram
english: "Your greatness, O mighty-armed son of Devakī, became known to me when the battle was upon us, and that sovereign form of yours as well."

sanskrit: yat tu tad bhavatā proktaṃ tadā keśava sauhṛdāt tat sarvaṃ puruṣavyāghra naṣṭaṃ me naṣṭacetasaḥ
english: "But that which you then declared, O Keśava, out of friendship — all of it, O tiger among men, is lost to me, for my mind was overthrown."

sanskrit: mama kautūhalaṃ tv asti teṣv artheṣu punaḥ prabho bhavāṃś ca dvārakāṃ gantā nacirād iva mādhava
english: "Yet I have a longing to hear those matters once again, O lord; and you, O Mādhava, will before long be setting out for Dvārakā."

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ phalgunaṃ pratyabhāṣata pariṣvajya mahātejā vacanaṃ vadatāṃ varaḥ
english: Thus addressed, Kṛṣṇa of great splendor, the best of speakers, embraced Phalguna and answered him with these words.

sanskrit: śrāvitas tvaṃ mayā guhyaṃ jñāpitaś ca sanātanam dharmaṃ svarūpiṇaṃ pārtha sarvalokāṃś ca śāśvatān
english: "By me you were made to hear the secret, O Pārtha, and were made to know the eternal Dharma in its own true nature, and all the everlasting worlds."

sanskrit: abuddhvā yan na gṛhṇīthās tan me sumahad apriyam nūnam aśraddadhāno 'si durmedhāś cāsi pāṇḍava
english: "That you did not grasp it, failing to understand, is a very great grief to me; surely you are wanting in faith, and dull of wit, O Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: sa hi dharmaḥ suparyāpto brahmaṇaḥ padavedane na śakyaṃ tan mayā bhūyas tathā vaktum aśeṣataḥ
english: "For that Dharma is fully sufficient for the knowing of the abode of Brahman; yet I cannot again declare it just so, in its entirety."

sanskrit: paraṃ hi brahma kathitaṃ yogayuktena tan mayā itihāsaṃ tu vakṣyāmi tasminn arthe purātanam
english: "For the supreme Brahman was then declared by me, joined as I was in yoga; but now I shall recount an ancient tale bearing upon that very matter."
